subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic core `sleep` tool that ends the current agent turn and resumes the same session after a bounded delay?
rationale: Current code has adjacent primitives but no generic sleep/resume API, and adding one would define new core tool, gateway lifecycle, cancellation, and possibly config policy.

options.title: Design Core Sleep Primitive
options.body: Add a bounded, non-durable sleep tool that reuses the existing turn-yield and wake machinery, with explicit cap and interruption tests.

options.title: Keep Existing Primitives
options.body: Leave cron, automatic completion wake, and `sessions_yield` as the supported patterns, then narrow or close this request as not planned.

options.title: Define Plugin/API Seam First
options.body: Create a runtime/plugin hook for delayed continuation before deciding whether a built-in core tool should exist.

recommendation.title: Design Core Sleep Primitive
recommendation.body: Add a bounded, non-durable sleep tool that reuses the existing turn-yield and wake machinery, with explicit cap and interruption tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting core/gateway product boundary decision, and recent history points to steipete for adjacent gateway/protocol and cron cleanup.
